title: Eight Evenings and One Open Question
subtitle: 思辨与辩论 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 思辨与辩论（生活与学习·思辨与表达）
meta: 主题语境：思辨与辩论（生活与学习·思辨与表达）　|　核心词汇：debate　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 debate 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1962 the chairman ① opened a debate that no society in the town would have scheduled, and he said the opening was the whole of the evening. The ② debate, meaning the arguing and not the motion, ran eight evenings and stayed unminuted; a debate, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unresolved.

Every ③ debate in that society had the same open question at the end of it, and the ④ debate at the end, meaning the one they kept for the visitors and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever attended twice. A debate, the secretary said, is nine parts listening and one part somebody willing to open; the chairman said the listening is the part that fills eight evenings.

The reporter meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the debate was the whole of the column, meaning the dispute and not the arguing. The ⑥ debate, meaning the dispute and not any of that, is the only thing in a column that everybody writes about and nobody settles; debate, he said, is either something you open or the only word that means both an arguing and a dispute. He said the dispute is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ debate had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the open question. The ⑧ debate of the whole thing, the chairman wrote in March, was one society and eight evenings of listening; debate, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to listen. She said the listening was never mentioned.

The ⑨ debate I remember is the one at the end, which was resumed in 1981 and is still described as the longest in the town. A ⑩ debate, the secretary said in 1983, is the only thing that improves by being argued; every debate, she said, is a dispute that has agreed to look like an arguing. She said the dispute was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 辩论；讨论（指学会里举行的那一场）
B. n. 辩论（指那种辩驳本身，与那个议题相对）
C. 固定搭配：open a debate 开启一场辩论
D. n. 辩论（指留给来访者举行的那一场）
E. n. 辩论；论辩（抽象总称，指一个学会的全部论辩）
F. n. 辩论（指节目单上写到、被排定的那一场）
G. n. 争论；争议（指专栏里报道的那一场）
H. n. 争议（抽象总称，指人人写却无人平息的那一场）

items.q: opened a debate that no society in the town would have scheduled
The debate, meaning the arguing and not the motion
the debate was the whole of the column
the debate had become a line in a programme
The debate of the whole thing
A debate, the secretary said in 1983

answers.why: open a debate 意为“开启一场辩论”，1962 年主席开启了一场全城没有一家学会肯排进日程的辩论。
debate 意为“辩论”，指那种辩驳本身而不是那个议题，它进行了八个晚上而没有记录。
debate 意为“辩论”，指那个学会里每一场辩论，每一场末尾都有同一个悬而未决的问题。
debate 意为“辩论”，指留给来访者举行的那一场，是唯一有人参加过两次的。
debate 意为“争论、争议”，指专栏里报道的那一场，记者说这场争议就是那个专栏的全部。
debate 意为“争议”，指人人写却无人平息的那一场而不是那种辩驳本身，是专栏里人人都写、却无人去平息的东西。
debate 意为“辩论”，指节目单上写到、被排定的那一场，到 1969 年这场辩论成了节目单里的一行。
debate 意为“辩论、论辩”，主席三月写道，整件事的论辩是一个学会和八个晚上的倾听。
debate 意为“辩论”，我记得的是末尾那一场，1981 年重启，至今仍被说成全城最长的一场。
debate 为抽象总称，秘书 1983 年说，一场辩论是唯一会因为被充分辩驳而变得更好的东西。
